outreach_angle: Josh, 4.8 stars across 134 reviews + 24/7 availability + a no-upsell rep is the kind of reputation most Vegas shops fake. But you have NO website I can find — you live entirely on Yelp and aggregator pages, so when someone Googles 'Josh The Bug Guy' they get a wall of third-party listings you don't control and can't convert. 21-day fix: a 3-page site (services / reviews / book-now) that ranks for your own name + an embedded review widget + a quote form = your 134-review reputation finally captures the searches it's already earning instead of feeding Yelp's ad machine.

Michael, 46 years family-owned + a bird/pigeon + solar-panel specialty is a moat almost nobody in Vegas has. But your Yelp shows only 15 photos and a thin review count for a 46-year business — you're under-telling the strongest story in the market. And the site doesn't lead with the pigeon/solar niche on the homepage hero. 30-day fix: hero rebuilt around '46 years + Vegas's pigeon & solar-panel pest experts' + a review-request SMS after every job (you've earned thousands, you're showing dozens) = four decades of credibility finally visible to every homeowner who Googles you.

AL Do It is doing the modern playbook right — own website, active Instagram, locally-owned 10+ years, anti-1-800-number positioning that resonates. But your reviews aren't surfacing on Google and the site has no scorpion or recurring-plan landing pages — the two highest-intent Vegas searches. 30-day fix: a 'scorpion control Las Vegas' page + a recurring quarterly-plan pricing page + Google review automation = the local-owner story you already tell on IG starts pulling search traffic that converts.

Annalisa, BBB A+ accreditation + a dedicated bee-removal specialty is rare positioning — live bee removal is a premium, low-competition niche worth $300-600 a call. But your web presence leans on BBB and directories, not a site that ranks for 'bee removal Las Vegas.' 21-day fix: a bee-removal landing page with your A+ badge + seasonal swarm-season content (Apr-Jun is your Black Friday) + a click-to-call hero = own the bee niche outright before swarm season peaks.

Boot A Pest has ~15 years of loyal NW-Vegas customers calling you 'on time and reliable' (Angi). But you're nearly invisible online — two different addresses listed across MapQuest, no website I can find, and almost no reviews for 15 years of work. 14-day fix: claim and unify your Google Business Profile to one address + a one-page site + a review-request text after each service = 15 years of goodwill stops leaking to competitors who simply show up first on the map.

Joslin, you've got a real site (mwpclv.com) and a clean Spring Valley book of business. But the site is thin — home / about / testimonials and not much that ranks. No service-specific pages, no neighborhood targeting, no recurring-plan pricing. 30-day fix: scorpion + general-pest + rodent service pages + a Spring Valley/Summerlin neighborhood page + quarterly-plan pricing = a site that actually pulls searches instead of just confirming you exist after someone already has your number.

Premier has served Clark County since 2001 — 25 years and 24/7 availability is a serious trust signal. But only ~10 Google reviews for a quarter-century business means newer competitors with 100+ reviews bury you in the map pack. 14-day fix: an automated post-service review request (text + email) + the '24 years serving Clark County' line in your hero and GBP = close the review gap that's the single thing keeping a 2001-founded shop off page one.

Darren, 5.0 stars + operating in the valley since 2004 + a real bed-bug specialty is a clean ICP win. But only 11 reviews means Henderson homeowners filtering for 25+ reviews never see you, and bed-bug is a high-ticket emergency search you should own. 21-day fix: a 'bed bug exterminator Henderson' landing page + review-request automation to get past 25 reviews in 90 days = a 22-year shop that finally ranks for its best, highest-margin service.
